newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on professional sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on professional sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold on Thursday slid below New York's Wednesday close on local and overseas professional selling, bullion traders said.
Professional dealers from Australia and in Hong Kong were selling the market in intraday trade, gold traders said.
"The whole market is just not convinced of any upward movement beyond US$380," said a gold dealer at an international bank.
Players still held onto short positions or were creating fresh short positions in anticipation of further drops, some dealers reported.
Support was seen at around $377 per ounce, but some felt gold may test $375 per ounce.
Physical buyers were wary of further price drops and were avoiding the market, dealers said.
"Physical buying took place only in dribs and drabs," said one gold dealer.
Bullion ended at US$377.85/378.35 an ounce on Thursday against New York's $378.20/80 close on Wednesday.
Local gold ended HK$2 lower at HK$3,485 a tael.
